Commentary.Commentary: The Sri Lankan bowlers will be aiming to fire on all cylinders and utilize the two-paced surface to the optimum. With around 95 overs left in the day, weather permitting, they will be backing themselves. Windies, on the other hand, don't need to panic. They have a capable batting line-up and the need of the hour for them is to remain composed. How will they react? Join us shortly on the other side.

The visitors are in this position courtesy a good batting display. Although, the start for them was a worrisome one. They had lost four wickets fairly early when they only had a 1-run lead but the 117-run stand between Dinesh Chandimal and Kusal Mendis brought them back on track. There was pressure on them but they thrived under it. The lower middle order came good as well. Brisk half centuries from Kusal Mendis and Niroshan Dickwella and useful knocks from Dinesh Chandimal and Roshen Silva put them in the ascendancy.

Shannon Gabriel leads his side off the field. He is getting a huge round of applause from his teammates and the crowd. An absolutely standout effort from the big man! 13 wickets in the game to be precise. The Windies hardly wasted any time to pick up the last two Sri Lankans wickets. However, amidst all this, Sri Lanka are way ahead in the context of the game.

OUT! BOOM! He is walking back now for sure. Gabriel looks unfazed by the wicket or still unhappy with the no ball two balls back. Whatever it was, he put it in his bowling. He has taken a 8-fer and has also reached 100 Test wickets, something which will please him a lot. Coming back to the ball, he bangs this one short, hits the deck hard and angles it into the body of the batsman. The variable bounce in the pitch means that the ball keeps low this time. Akila looks to duck under it but gets hits on his hanging bat and the ball crashes into the stumps. It's the end of the Sri Lankan innings and the Windies need 296 runs to win this Test match.
Outside off, on a drivaeable length, the left-hander plants his foot down the pitch and hits it through cover-point. Roston Chase cuts it out and keeps it down to two.

What? Are you kidding me? Another no ball and another wicket. I can't really figure out if he's lucky to have picked up a 12-fer or unlucky to have missed out on taking 15 wickets in the match. Full and on the stumps, Dananjaya moves away from his stumps to hit it through the line but gets an inside edge. The ball disturbs the furniture after taking the deflection off the bat. But Ian Gould has his right arm up and signals for a no ball. Not much Gabriel can do as he walks back to his run up.
Short and incoming from the angle, Akila hits it up and over the slip cordon. The ball lobs in the air and thuds into the ground at third man region. Two runs are taken as a result.
Hangs back and punches the shortish delivery to the right of the bowler.
Another swings and miss from Kumara. He survives another over.
The ball is way wide on the leg side but the batsman still goes after it.
Gets back and keeps the back of a length ball out.
A play and a miss. Outside off, on a fuller length and goes past the outside edge of the blade.
The batsman has worked it off his pads behind square. One more run added to the lead.
Full around off from around the wicket from Roach. Akila lifts it over the fielder at mid off and runs two. Some intent from the last pair, just after the fall of wicket.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Lahiru Kumara is the last man in.

OUT! Yes, he's gone! Lakmal is right in front of the stumps and the umpire has no hesitation in raising the finger. Gabriel has his 7th of the innings and 12th in the match. He goes fuller and angles it into the right-hander. Lakmal plays down the wrong line off the back foot and is hit on his pads. It looks dead to the naked eye but Suranga goes for a review in desperation, after some discussions with his non-striker. The Ultra Edge doesn't spot anything. Time for the Hawk Eye. It shows that the ball would have hit the top of the leg stump and he has to go. Nice early breakthrough for Windies, just what the doctor ordered! Gabriel has produced the best-ever bowling figures in a match by a Windies bowler at home. He has beaten Sir Curtly Ambrose, who had 11 wickets.
Suranga Lakmal has been trapped in front but he has decided to challenge the decision. Looks like he is a goner.
Errs in line this time and bowls it down the leg side.
Even fuller around the same area and invites the drive. Lakmal misses the ball.
Goes fuller around off, pushed to the off side.
A back of a length to starts things on Day 5. The batsman gets behind the line and blocks it.

We are set to get rolling. Akila Dananjaya and Suranga Lakmal to resume their innings. Shannon Gabriel, the star for the Windies, to start the proceedings with the ball. Three slips and a gully in place. Here we go...

PITCH REPORT - Russel Arnold assessing the surface says that Akila Dananjaya will be the key for Sri Lanka in the fourth innings. He explains that Roston Chase extracted good purchase from the good length area around the off stump of the right-handed batsmen and Dananjaya needs to be consistent as well. States that the track still looks good if the batsmen decide to apply themselves. Ends by saying that we have an exciting finish in our hands.

Jeff Dujon is talking to West Indies head coach Stuart Law, who says they need to be positive and show intent. He adds that he'd like a big positive effort from his bowlers. He praises his bowlers and says that Cummins, Roach and others bowled well but the pick of the bowlers was Gabriel. He emphasizes that they need to remain positive as they will be chasing a big total, and a good platform laid by the top order can make things better for the batsmen to follow. He concludes by saying that the conditions are good for batting and bowling. He says that the pitch flattened out in the third and fourth day but the unevenness is there, which makes things even more interesting.

The thing in favour of the hosts is that they are 1-0 up in the series and that will help them to plan out the way they want to play. Will the Windies show resilience? Or will the Sri Lankans dominate the proceedings and level the series? This game is heading towards a thrilling finish. Let's hope the rain doesn't play a spoilsport.

Hello and a warm welcome to the final day of the second Test. The Sri Lankans have batted extremely well to land themselves in a commanding position. Their lead stands at 287 at the moment. It is to be seen whether they have decided to declare or they still want to add some useful runs to ensure that they can't lose this game. Windies, on the other hand, need to believe in themselves. Time and again we have seen in cricket that whenever a side gives its best, tides can change pretty quickly.
... Final Day, Session 1 ...

Day 5 of this Test match promises to be an enthralling one. It is to be seen whether Sri Lanka declare overnight or continue to bat on. It is already a very good score on a pitch which has started to deteriorate. The Windies will be aiming to come out on a fresh note and clean up the tail as quickly as possible. After that, they have their task cut out and are bound to be tested. Catch us on Monday for all the action. Till then, Ciao!

For the hosts, Shannon Gabriel was the pick of the bowlers as he picked up a 6-fer in this innings and has 11 wickets in the match so far. Kemar Roach got two as well but other than these two, no other bowler really troubled the Sri Lankan batsmen. The pitch looks slow but there is still enough on it for those who are willing to bend their backs and shell it out, as shown by Gabriel.

Great day for Sri Lanka! They are in the driving seat now. Their batsmen have done a marvelous job to come back from 48/4 to 334/8. The middle lower order came to the party and took the advantage away from the home team. Kusal Mendis, Dinesh Chandimal, Roshen Silva and Niroshan Dickwella played crucial knocks, put on important partnerships and kept the Windies bowlers at bay for as long as possible. They played and missed many a time but didn't let it affect them or their batting. At the end of the day's play, they still have two batsmen fighting it out and looking to swell the lead, which is 287 runs at the moment.

Four Leg Byes! Full delivery, slipping down the leg side. Dananjaya tries to glance it away but the ball brushes his pads and flies past the keeper to reach the ropes. Umpire Aleem Dar takes a reading again and decides to call it a day. THAT'S STUMPS ON DAY 4!
Fuller length ball on middle and leg, defended tentatively off the front foot.
On a length outside off, played with an open bat face towards point.
Another short ball, takes off after pitching. Akila sits under it.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Bouncer from Holder, Dananjaya sits underneath it.
Leg bye! Pitching outside the leg stump as Akila tries to flick it away but is hit on the pads. The ball rolls towards fine leg and a run is taken.
Well played! Overpitched outside off, creamed through covers for a brace.
Error in judgement! Back of a length ball aimed at the body, Akila points his bat skywards and takes a blow on his arm guard. He needs to be careful.
Leg bye! Angling in from a good length. Suranga hops to defend it but the ball hits his thigh pad and just lobs over the short leg fielder. The batsmen take a run.
Cummins loses his radar and slips this one way down the leg side. Lakmal tries to glance it but misses.
Back of a length outside off, left alone.
Here comes, what looks like a light meter. Aleem Dar checks the reading and it seems good enough to continue the play. Meanwhile, Miguel Cummins takes the ball in his hand for his spell.
Swinging down the leg side, Akila tries to work it away but misses.
Back of a length ball leaving the southpaw. He shuffles across and lets it be.
Back of a length on middle and leg, Lakmal turns it through backward square leg to rotate strike.

The ball falls in no man's land! A well-directed bouncer by Holder. Lakmal swings across the line without watching the ball and gets a top edge over the keeper. He sprints after it to catch it but the ball falls down safely. A couple taken.
Similar length ball, shaping in, defended stoutly off the back foot.
Back of a length ball around off, kept out watchfully.
FOUR! Delightful! Fuller length ball, angling away from Dananjaya. He takes a stride forward and caresses it nicely through cover-point to find the fence.
Angling across Dananjaya. He tries to hit it away but misses.
The batsman works it down the leg side. One run added to the total.

Safe! Yes, the impact is well outside the line! Shaping in prodigiously from a good length outside off. Lakmal with minimal feet movement tries to whack it through covers but misses to get hit on the flap of the pad. Gabriel appeals but the umpire shakes his head. Holder looks at his bowler and decides to challenge the decision after some thinking. The Hawk Eye rolls in. Well, the impact is outside off and that is the end of the story.
An LBW appeal against Suranga Lakmal has been taken upstairs. Seems like the impact was outside the line.
Short of a length ball, tucked through mid-wicket for a run.
On a driveable length around off, Akila tries to drive it through the line but only manages to play it off the inner half back to the bowler.
As expected, Holder bowls this one on the leg stump with a leg slip in place. Akila plays it tentatively towards backward square leg and takes a single.
Leg slip comes into place now.

FOUR! The runs continue to come for Sri Lanka! Still something in this pitch as proved on this occasion. This one takes off from a length on middle and leg and lands Dananjaya in an awkward position. He tries to fend it away but the ball brushes his gloves and goes past the diving Dowrich to reach the fine leg fence.
Good length ball outside off, Suranga places it towards backward point and takes a brisk single.
A gentle pitched up delivery outside off, swinging away. Lakmal leans ahead and blocks it.
A good yorker outside off, Lakmal is alert to it and jams it out towards covers.
Shortish delivery outside off, shaping in. Suranga has a go at it but fails to connect.
Jason Holder brings himself on.
Full ball on the pads, nudged round the corner for a run.
No ball! Another one, I have lost count of them. Fuller ball outside off, moving away. Lakmal pushes at it but gets beaten. That was a tight call for overstepping though.
Short of a length delivery, defended stoutly from within the crease.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Shortish ball around off, Akila tries to ramp it over the keeper but misses.
Fuller length ball on middle, Lakmal tries to clip it away but is early into his shot. Ends up getting a leading edge through covers and a single is taken.
Suranga Lakmal is the new man in.

OUT! 6-fer for Gabriel! He continues to rule the roost at home. A tame dismissal to say the least! Can't blame it though as this is the way he plays. Gabriel runs in from around the wicket and attacks the stumps with a full length delivery. Dickwella makes room and tries to play it over covers but doesn't get any sort of timing behind it. The ball flies towards extra cover where Kieran Powell accepts it gleefully. An entertaining knock from Dickwella nonetheless. He gets a round of applause from his teammates.
Back of a length ball in line of the stumps, turned to the leg side for a single.

FOUR! All these runs matter and the lead continues to climb, 260 to be precise! Shortish ball outside off, Dickwella flashes at it but gets an outside edge over the slip cordon to earn himself another boundary.
Beaten! Back of a length ball well outside off, Dickwella takes a late call to ramp it over the slip cordon but only manages to connect with thin air.
Fuller in length in that tight off stump corridor, Dickwella pushes it towards covers.
Good length ball around off, kept out watchfully.
In line of the stumps, Dickwella covers the line and plays it towards mid-wicket.
Similar length ball, turned through mid-wicket for a run.
Short of a length ball directed at the body, Dananjaya fends it off past short leg and takes a run.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Dug in short, Akila ducks under it.
Short of a length ball on middle and leg, tucked past short leg for a couple of runs.
Akila Dananjaya strides out to bat.

OUT! It is off the gloves! What an outstanding catch. Take a bow, Shane Dowrich. Consecutive 5-wicket hauls in this match for Shannon Gabriel as well, he has been on fire throughout. The hosts needed this wicket badly and it is the second new ball which has come to their rescue. Gabriel bowls this one in the avenue of apprehension and gets the ball to nip in from a length. Silva comes forward tentatively to counter it but it seems that the ball brushes his gloves and flies behind. Dowrich moves swiftly to his left and leaps like a goalkeeper to grab a stunner with his left hand. The Windies appeal and up goes the umpire's finger. However, Silva has a confused look on his face. He is indicating to Dickwella that it might have touched his elbow. Takes the review after some deliberation. The Snicko rolls in and it spots a deflection off the glove. The on-field decision stays. That is the end of a good innings from Roshen Silva, he misses out on his fifty by a couple of runs. That also closes the 99-run stand, a stand which has put Sri Lanka in the ascendancy. The tourists lead by 251 runs.
Roshen Silva has been caught behind but he feels that the ball has deflected off his elbow. He conveys that to his partner and finally challenges the decision. Let us find out...
Shannon Gabriel is back to share the second new ball.
That's a peach! Pitches on a length in the corridor of uncertainty and moves away at the last moment to go past the hanging bat of Dickwella.
Well played! Short and width on offer, Dickwella slashes it over the point region and comes back for a couple of runs.
Back of a length outside off, Niroshan mistimes his punch towards covers.

A loose shot! Perhaps, he has the cushion behind him to go for a few extravagant strokes. That is the way he plays as well. On a driveable length outside off and there is room as well. Dickwella throws his bat at it but fails to connect.
Almost a replica of the previous delivery as Dickwella leaves it again.
This one is wide outside off and Dickwella doesn't bother to play at it.

The second new ball is due now and it has been taken with immediate effect. Kemar Roach has been given the responsibility with the brand new cherry. Will it bring a change in fortunes for the home side? Let's wait and watch.
Floated outside off, played with soft hands to covers for a single.
Silva goes deep in his crease and turns it through square leg for a run. Lead moves to 250 for Sri Lanka.
Leans ahead to the tossed up ball and eases it through covers to rotate strike.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Curs this one away towards backward point for a brisk run.

9th Test fifty for Dickwella! Tossed up outside off, he tries to push it through the line but gets it off the outer half past the gully region. Some aggressive running between the wickets allows the batsmen to come back for the third run. This is also the first time a Sri Lankan wicket-keeper has scored a half ton in the Caribbean. He looks towards the heavens and gets a good round of applause from the Sri Lankan dressing room. A crucial knock in the context of the game.
A little bit of hydration for the umpires. Meanwhile Roston Chase is brought into the attack.
Loopy delivery, worked to the man at mid on.
Silva decides to use his feet but he is not quite to the pitch of the ball. Ends up defending it.
Slow through the air, eased off the front foot towards mid on.
FOUR! Poor delivery and duly punished! A half-tracker on off, Silva rocks back and pulls it with the spin through mid on. A boundary results. The lead moves onto 242.
Shorter in length, kept out with ease off the back foot.
Tossed up delivery, played with the spin to mid-wicket.
Kraigg Brathwaite comes into the attack. A rather surprising change.
Leg bye! Angling down the leg side, Silva fails to flick it away. The ball brushes his pads and rolls to the leg side. A single taken.
Short of a length outside off, the batsman points his bat skywards and leaves it alone.
Full delivery outside off, Roshen Silva leans ahead and defends it nicely down the track.
Nicely directed shortish ball around off, shaping in. Silva arches his back, drops his wrists and lets it go safely.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
No ball! This is the second time in a row Cummins has overstepped. 9th no ball in the innings for the Windies. Dug in short, Roshen ducks under it.
No ball! Perhaps, Dickwella heard the call from the umpire and that is why he chose to play the same shot with a fielder near the third man fence. Goes to him on the bounce and a run is taken.

FOUR! Innovative! The wicket-keeper batsman is unorthodox but is mighty effective when he is in flow. Shortish ball angling in from around the wicket, Dickwella ramps it nicely over the slip cordon and earns himself a boundary.
Shows the full face of the bat to the tossed up ball and blocks it right under his eyes.
Ooh! That one kept extremely low. A bit shorter outside off, Silva shapes to cut it away but is beaten by the lack of bounce. That was not far from the off stump.
Fullish ball around off, patted back towards the bowler.
Dickwella brings out the sweep again and plays it towards deep square leg for a run.
Quicker and flatter outside off, punched off the back foot to the off side.

FOUR! Here comes the sweep and it has been played to great effect. Fullish delivery around off, a good shot selection from Dickwella as he decides to broom it away through backward square leg. The connection is good and the ball races to the fence.
A play and a miss! This is the corridor where the hosts should be striving to bowl more often. On a fuller length outside off, seaming in. Silva comes forward tentatively to block it but gets foxed.
Well-directed bouncer on off. It is fiery and fast as Silva ducks under it in a flash.
Shortish ball outside off, the batsman doesn't have a go at it.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Good take from Dowrich! Slipping down the leg side, Roshen tries to glance it but misses. The ball brushes his thigh pad and goes behind. The keeper flies to his left to take a great stop.
Short of a length outside off, played with an angled blade towards gully. Shouts a loud NO to his partner.
Silva is nimble on his feet to the quicker one and knocks it down to long on. A run taken.
Strides forward confidently to this one and pushes it towards mid off.
Full delivery on off, kept out watchfully.
Outside off, eased to the covers for a single.
Tossed up delivery on middle, Roshen clears his front leg and places it towards cover-point for a run.
Floated outside off, Roshen hangs back and blocks it towards covers.
Outside off, left alone.

With a majority off side field, Cummins bowls this one down the leg side. Not the line he should be bowling. Dickwella turns it around the corner and picks up a couple. The hosts can't afford to give away easy runs.
Third man comes into position now. It's a 7-2 field with the offside being the packed side. Windies are changing the tactics perhaps, in search of a breakthrough.

FOUR! Just out of the reach of the fielder! Back of a length ball outside off, angling in and takes off a touch. Dickwella is cramped for room but guides it towards the gully region. Hope there leaps but the ball flies past him in a flash to reach the fence.
In the channel outside off, left alone.
FOUR! Crisp! That flew off the bat. Fractionally overpitched outside off, Dickwella leans ahead and drives it on the up through covers. The timing is spot on and the ball whistles away to the fence.

This is sensible stuff from the duo! Good running. Good length ball, shaping in sharply. Silva tries to work it away but gets an inside edge onto his pads. The ball rolls towards cover-point and the batsmen pinch a single.
Goes deep in the crease and places it towards point for a run.
Tossed up delivery well outside off, Dickwella with a high backlift caresses it through covers. The fielder runs after it and manages to save a run for his side.
Driven through the covers by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Oohs and Aahs from the Windies! Quick and accurate delivery, Roshen rocks back and is a bit late on it but manages to cut it to point.
Drifting in on a fuller length, Silva puts his head down and defends it calmly.
Pushed quicker through the air and spinning away. Silva tries to cut it away but gets beaten.
Close shave! Angling in sharply from a back of a length outside off, Dickwella is late to bring his bat down as the ball passes under his bat and goes past the off stump.
Drinks has been called. Time for a breather, and regroup for the last burst of the evening session.

No ball! The problem of overstepping continues to haunt the Windies. This is the seventh no ball of the innings. There were a couple of times when they had got the better of the batsmen but it doesn't count. Down the leg side, helped away towards fine leg for a couple of runs.
Back of a length delivery, defended solidly off the back foot.
Short delivery directed at the rib cage area of the batsman. He tucks it nicely towards short mid-wicket.
Back of a length ball around off, the wicket-keeper batsman hops and pats it towards mid on.
Length ball outside off, Dickwella shuffles across and defends it stoutly.
Cummins runs in from around the wicket and pitches it full around off. Dickwella pushes at it but ends up getting it off the outer half towards gully.
Miguel Cummins comes back into the attack.
250 up for Sri Lanka! Makes use of the depth of the crease and places it through covers for a single.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

Spinning into Dickwella who turns it through square leg for a brace. That brings up the 50-run partnership between the duo. They have brought themselves into a position of ascendancy on a tricky surface.
Low full toss on middle, helped away through mid-wicket for a run. The lead for Sri Lanka touches 200. Good going from them.
Shorter in length outside off, guided to third man for a couple of runs.
Bishoo sees Silva giving charge and attacks the stumps. The batsman ends up yorking himself but is able to jam it out.
Full and targeting the stumps, the batsman punches it with the full face of the bat and gets it down the ground. The fielder runs after it and cuts it down to three.
Roach goes full well outside off, Silva throws his bat at it, gets it nicely from the middle but couldn't get it past the fielder at covers.
Outside off and left alone by Silva.
On a length outside off, a tentative punch to covers off the back foot.
Full around off and driven to mid off for nothing.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Quicker delivery around leg, the batsman looks to flicks it fine but misses and gets hit on his pad once again.
Pitches it outside and brings it in to the left-hander. The ball spins and hits the pads of Dickwella.
Gives this one enough air near the off stump and spins it away from the face of the bat. The ball takes the shoulder of the bat and rolls towards third man. One run is added to the total.
Copy past stuff from the bowler and the batsman.
Floater around middle and leg, Silva is happy to block it off the front foot.
Flighted around off, spinning away and the batsman tucks it behind point for a brace.

Dropped and a run out chance missed! Oh goodness! It seemed that the intensity was dropping and that might have caused this. Shortish ball outside off, Silva flashes hard at it but gets a thick outside edge that flies towards gully. Shai Hope stationed there leaps to his left and is in a decent position to take it as well. However, the ball bursts out of his hands and rolls behind. The batsmen set off for the run. Bishoo is aware of the situation and attacks the stumps at the bowler's end coming from point. Misses the shy though as Silva struggles to make his crease. The replays show that if there was a direct hit, the batsman was not even in the frame. Roach could have collected it and thrown it at the stumps as well. A chance goes down abegging.
Back of a length delivery, defended off the back foot.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
No ball! Outside off, Roshen lets it go. Roach has overstepped by a long margin. There is certainly a drop in intensity from the Windies.
Good game awareness! On a good length outside off, Niroshan taps it towards cover-point and pinches a brisk single.
Streaky but effective! Full length ball attacking the stumps, Niroshan goes for a heave but gets it off the inner half through mid-wicket. A couple of runs are taken.
Back of a length outside off, played with an angled bat towards point.
On a flatter trajectory, turned from deep within the crease towards square leg for a single.
Slow through the air, driven against the spin through mid on to rotate strike.

Some lousy stuff from Roach! Full delivery outside off, Silva eases it through covers and takes a run. Kemar stationed near the ropes doesn't budge even an inch and Powell has to run after it. Hence, an extra run results.
Straighter one from Bishoo. Roshen leans ahead in defense.
Floated ball around off, spinning away. Silva keeps his bat inside the line and lets it be.
Short and quick around off, tapped nicely towards short third man for a single.
Angling in sharply this time on a fuller length, played defensively towards the leg side.
Too far to make the batsman play and he remains circumspect in approach.
Once again this is well outside off. Roshen doesn't fiddle with it.
Fuller in length this time and a bit closer to the batsman who tucks it towards mid on.
Well outside off, left alone.
Bowls this one wide outside off, ignored by the batsman.
Change of ends for Kemar Roach.
Bishoo drags his length back and Niroshan defends it down the pitch.
Slow through the air, defended solidly off the front foot.
Nicely played! On a flatter trajectory and quick in pace, Niroshan knows where the gap is. He dabs it late through short third man and comes back for a couple.
Waits for the ball to spin into him and turns it around the corner for a run.
Shorter in length, ample time for Dickwella to punch it past the diving mid on fielder. A run taken.
Down the leg side, tucked through square leg for a single.
Gabriel is going back to the dressing room after his spell. Perhaps, to take a breather. Meanwhile, Devendra Bishoo is back for a bowl.
Similar length into the stumps, flicked to the leg side for another single.

Dishes a fuller ball outside off and entices the right-hander to go for the drive. The ball moves away just a touch after pitching and Silva does well to read that. He opens the face of his bat to guide it behind. The ball goes past to the right of the gully fielder and two runs are taken.

Nice! Beautiful looking punch off the back foot from Silva. Gets a short and wide delivery and hangs back to put it through cover-point region. Slow outfield means the ball is stopped inside the ropes and two runs are taken.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Leg Bye! Back of a length from 'round the wicket, Dickwella looks to flick but gets wrapped on the thigh pad. One run is taken in the end.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Goes fuller and still targets his stumps. Silva hangs back and somehow manages to keep it out.
Wide down the leg side, the batsman leaves it alone.
Back of a length outside off, the batsman wants to flick it to the leg side but is beaten.
Drags back his length a touch and targets the stumps. Silva is happy to block it out.
Touch fuller and another resolute defense from Silva.
Back of a length around off, blocked off the front foot.
Kemar Roach is back on.

A loud appeal for an LBW is turned down! Full around middle and leg and hits Dickwella on his pads. The bowler is appealing his heart out but the umpire isn't moving. He goes to his skipper to plead him for the review. But the skipper is unmoved as well. Gabriel isn't happy. The replays show that it would have been umpire's call as the ball just clipped the leg stump.

FOUR! He can bat, mind you! Gabriel tests him with an incoming short delivery and Dickwella stays put in his crease and slices it over the gully fielder for a boundary. He holds his pose for the cameras.
Back of a length around the ribs of the left-hander who tucks it to the leg side for nothing.
Bye! Full around off and another one which keeps low. Silva lets one through to the keeper but it bounces before him and evades him. The ball goes behind him and one run is taken.
There is a man at a catching position at short mid-wicket.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Keeps it on a full length on the stumps and Silva guides to the leg side for nothing.
Full outside off and a nice looking drive but straight to covers.
Gets behind the line and blocks it.
Drags his length back, keeps it outside off and Dickwella goes after it. The ball keeps rising and goes past the outside edge.
Full around off, the batsman punches with hard hands and almost hits it straight to the fielder.
Wide outside off, left alone again.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.

FOUR! Full and angled on his pads and sweetly clipped over the mid-wicket region. The ball has enough legs to reach the boundary. Silva remained unfazed by the previous delivery and that is a good sign for the visitors.

That virtually crept down the pitch and it was bowled at 140 kph! On a good length around off and stays ever so low. Silva hangs his bat in anticipation but it misses his bat and the off stump. Pitch is playing its part here in St Lucia.
On a good length outside off, Silva gets near the pitch of the delivery and turns it to gully with the outside half of the bat.
Drags his length back, too wide and left alone by the batsman.
Almost a yorker to back it up. Gabriel is targeting the stumps now. The batsman does well to keep it out.
Full and on middle and off, Roshen gets behind the line and blocks it.
The umpires are once again having a look at the ball. Seems that we will have another change. Yes, the fourth umpire runs in with a box full of balls.
Holder gets closer to the off stump and Dickwella plants his foot down the pitch to push it through covers. Two runs are taken to end the over.
On a good length outside off, the batsman reaches for it from his crease and gets it from the inside half down the pitch.
Wide outside off, left alone by Dickwella.
Similar line and length and tucked to the leg side for nothing.
Back of a length on middle and leg, the batsman flicks to the on side and changes strike.
Wide down the leg side, the batsman leaves it alone.
Full around off and driven through covers for a couple.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.

FOUR! Almost another one. Dishes this one full around off and invites the drive from the left-hander. He gets a thick outside edge and the ball flies between gully and slip cordon. No one moved and the ball races to the fence for a boundary. 200 up for Sri Lanka.
The batsman has driven the full ball straight down the ground.
Niroshan Dickwella is the new man in.

OUT! Rattled! A very, very important wicket for the home side. Gabriel didn't bowl in the last session and he comes back to provide the breakthrough straightaway. From wide of the crease, he angles the ball into to the right-hander, on a good length and it seams in after pitching. Mendis gets his bat down at an angle and also plays away from his body which proves to be his undoing. Ends up chopping it onto his stumps. The umpire checks upstairs regarding Gabriel has overstepped or not. On one occasion he had done so at a crucial stage but this time he is on the money. Kusal is shattered. He was playing really well but now he has to go. The visitors are ahead by 152 runs.
Class! Short and wide and nicely punched off the back foot through backward point. Mendis adds two to Sri Lanka's total.
Shannon Gabriel to bowl from the other end.
Drives to mid off for nothing.
Similar line and length, Silva flicks it off his hips and takes two.
Touch too straight and hits him on the pads.
Some swing in the air, outside off, Silva keeps his bat close to his body.
Outside off, left alone.

Bye! Starts with a gentle loosener down the leg side. The keeper fails to collect it. Appeal from Holder and he is backed up by the Snicko as well but there was clear daylight between bat and ball. One run taken from the fine leg region.

So, here we are again. Building up for the final phase of play. The sun is shining in all its glory and we want it to stay the same way. There are still 44 overs that can be roped in today. Jason Holder to steam in first up. Here we go...
Update 1507 Local - Everything seems alright. The pitch, the weather and the outfield. We are set to begin in about 8 minutes.
Update 1455 Local - An inspection has been scheduled in 5 minutes. Hopefully, play will resume soon.
Update 1440 Local - We should have got underway now but the outfield hasn't completely dried up yet and hence, the start is delayed as the mopping up is being done. Stay with us for further updates.
... Day 4, Session 3 ...

Early Tea has been taken due to the stoppage. A session which puts Sri Lanka in front and with Kusal Mendis in the middle, they can call the shots in the game now. Kemar Roach sent Dinesh Chandimal home earlier in the session, however, their other bowlers were wayward in their approach. It has been a snail-paced cricket with regular intervals due to something or the other. If the visitors are able to extend their lead up to 200, it will be a tough task for the home team. Surprisingly, Shannon Gabriel didn't bowl in this session. Jason Holder might have missed a trick here. Or was it a tactical decision? Catch us after the break for the evening session to find out.

Update 1405 Local - Covers are on the field. Dark clouds are looming just behind the stadium and it doesn't look too good. The weather has been switching on and off for a while now and ultimately, it has started to drizzle. Let's u hope its a passing shower. Stay tuned for further updates.

There is an issue once again. The umpires are having a look at Roshen Silva's bat. He had taken the sticker out of his bat. So, he is being asked to tape that area as it is sticky and affecting the ball.
Short ball, pulled away to the leg side for a single.

In the air... but safe! Another nervy moment but Mendis survives. Back of a length ball down the leg side, Mendis is early into his tuck and hence, gets a top edge that balloons over the pitch. Cummins and Hope (gully) run in to catch the ball but the ball falls down safely, tantalizingly close to the striker's end. The bowler has a wry smile on his face.
Shortish ball outside off, cut away through point for a couple.
In the channel outside off, left alone.
Back of a length ball, angling in, Mendis makes use of the depth of the crease and defends it solidly.
Good length ball outside off, Kusal points his bat skywards to let it be.
Time for Drinks.
Length ball on off, defended solidly off the back foot.

Nervy moment! In the corridor of uncertainty, coming in with the natural angle. Silva comes half-forward to deal with it but is late to bring his bat down. The ball goes under his bat and just misses the off stump.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Full length ball around off, driven crisply towards mid off.
Outside off, left alone.
Length ball on middle and leg, Mendis helps it through mid-wicket for a single.
Wide! Short and it is way down the leg side. Mendis lets it go. Wide signaled by the umpire.
Full and straight on this occasion, clipped nicely through mid-wicket for a brace.
Back of a length outside off, Roshen mistimes his cut shot towards point.
That is a jaffa! Pitched on a length outside off and straightens. Silva pushes at it tamely and gets foxed.
In the channel outside off, left alone.
Hops in the crease and tucks it to the leg side for a run.

Safe! Just by an inch though! Mendis would have had his heart in his mouth. Fullish delivery in line of the stumps, Silva tries to flick it away but gets it off the inner half through backward square leg. Bishoo hares after it to keep the ball in play. The batsmen after having ran a couple hesitate a touch. The throw comes in towards Dowrich as Mendis dives in desperately to come back in. Dowrich flicks off the bails and appeals. Seems really close. The replays roll in. Well, Mendis has just about made his crease. Would have been a heartbreaking moment for Sri Lanka had he not.
That looks pretty close! A run out appeal against Mendis has been referred upstairs. Is he short of his crease?
Miguel Cummins comes back for a bowl.
Hangs back to the back of the length ball and defends it nicely.
Dug in short, ducked under comfortably.
FOUR! Hammered! Short ball halfway down the pitch from Holder. Mendis stands tall and pulls it hard past the square leg fielder for a rocketing boundary.
Slightly overpitched outside off, pushed off the front foot towards mid off.
Fuller in length on middle and leg, kept out watchfully.
Good length ball on leg stump, defended beside the pitch on the leg side.
Jason Holder is back on.
Good length ball outside off, holding its line. Silva points his bat skywards to let it be.
Slightly overpitched outside off, driven on the up through covers for a couple.
Roach is probing around that off stump channel. This one is on the off stump and stays a bit low. Roshen does well to camp back and block it.
Shaping in substantially on a fuller length from outside off. Roshen knows where his off stump is and makes a good leave.
Full on middle and leg, Kusal tucks it in front of square leg to rotate strike.
Roach attempts a bouncer but it is not well-directed. It is down the leg side as Mendis ducks under it comfortably.
Slower through the air, worked away towards mid-wicket for a run.
Nicely done! Short delivery well outside off, Silva cuts it late towards third man and picks up three runs for doing so.
Tossed up around leg stump, Roshen opts to pad it away. Not a risky thing to do so as it was spinning down leg as well.
Spinning into Silva who tucks it with soft hands to the same region.
Clipped with the spin towards mid-wicket.
On middle and leg, played defensively towards the leg side.
Short delivery and a lot of room on offer, Mendis slashes at it but misses.
Good length ball, defended solidly off the back foot.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman.

SIX! What a shot! He is very strong at anything which is on his pads. He stays stable and whips the fullish delivery over square leg for a maximum. Geez! Brilliant timing and he has also got a good bat with him.
In the channel outside off, left alone.
Back of a length ball, shaping in sharply. Mendis covers his off stump and lets it go.

The umpires are having a look at the ball. They go towards Jason Holder and are having a serious discussion with him. Now, together they go towards Roshen Silva. They are checking his bat, perhaps thinking there might be something which has been applied on it. The batsman calls in for a new bat. And the ball has been changed as well. A lot is happening.
Plants his foot down the pitch and keeps it out to the on side.
Pushed in with the angle and nicely defended by the batsman off the back foot.
Gets on the front foot and flicks it to the fielder at mid-wicket for nothing.
A touch flatter in trajectory, Silva stays put and keep it out.
Flighted around off, Mendis comes down the track and pushes it through mid on for a single.
Loopy delivery around off, the batsman stays behind the line and defends it.
Played to mid-wicket region by the batsman.
In the channel outside off, left alone.
Roshen Silva is the new man in.

OUT! You bet! This is a massive, massive wicket for the Windies! They are over the moon. They had missed a trick when they didn't review a caught behind appeal against Mendis but this time they have got it right. Coming back to the delivery, it is on a shortish length outside off which tempts Chandimal to go for an audacious shot. He does oblige and tries to cut it square of the wicket on the off side but the ball doesn't bounce as much he expected. Hence, the ball seems to have gone just under his bat and carries to Dowrich who takes it and appeals confidently. The rest of the team is in sync with him as well. Holder does challenge the decision. The replays roll in. Oh yes! The Ultra Edge shows a big spike as the ball goes past his bat. There is enough evidence to overturn the decision. OUT flashes on the giant screen. After riding his luck on a few occasions, the Sri Lankan skipper is walking back in disappointment. The 117-run stand has been broken. Sri Lanka are ahead by 118 runs with only 5 wickets in the kitty.

Can be a big moment in the game! Windies review a caught behind decision against Chandimal. The body language of the players is confident. Holder consults with his teammates and challenges the decision. Is there an edge?
Full ball on the pads, clipped nicely through mid-wicket for a brace.
Length delivery around off, stays a bit low. Dinesh keeps it out watchfully.

Brilliant work! Good commitment shown. Short and room on offer, Chandimal pounces on it with a slap towards covers but Blackwood is sharp as a hawk. He dives to his right like a goalkeeper and saves a boundary for his side.
Around off, spinning in, worked around the corner for a run. Sensible batting.
Leans ahead and taps the floated ball towards mid-wicket.
Spinning into Dinesh who defends it beside the pitch on the leg side.
Spinning down the leg side, Mendis tries to work it away but gets it off the inner half towards short fine leg. A run taken.
Nicely played! Once again it is shorter in length. Chandimal has ample time to rock back and cuts it through point. The fielder hares after it and saves a run for his side.
Shorter in length, Mendis goes for the sweep but gets an under edge towards short fine leg. A single taken.

FOUR! First boundary for Chandimal in this innings! Quite a safe shot this. Shortish and width on offer, Chandimal throws his bat at it and gets a thick outside edge which goes over the slip cordon for a boundary.
Well bowled! In the avenue of apprehension, shaping in. Chandimal knows where his off stump is and makes an assured leave.
Short of a ball around off, defended with a straight bat.
Short of a length ball outside off, keeps a touch low. Chandimal leaves it alone as the ball bounces twice before reaching the keeper.
This one is fuller just outside the off stump, Dinesh leans ahead and defends it calmly down the track.
On a length, shaping in from outside off. Chandimal reaches the pitch of the delivery and blocks it right under his eyes.
Chandimal clears his front leg and Chase follows him. Knocked down nicely through mid on for a single.
Slower through the air, the Sri Lankan skipper lunges forward in defense.
Erring in line as the ball goes down the leg side, Mendis helps it away to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Chandimal is nimble on his feet and works it down to long on to rotate strike.
Tossed up on a fuller length outside off, Dinesh eases it to covers.
On middle and leg, kept out towards short leg.
Roach goes wider of the crease and angles this one in. Mendis defends it with his bat and pad close together.
On a length around off, a bit of nibble in the air. Kusal is opened up a bit in his stance but manages to defend it.
Outside off, left alone.
Peach! Pitches on a length in the corridor of uncertainty and moves away late to go past the hanging bat of Mendis.

SIX! That is a shot of a man in prime form! Full length ball, angling in. Mendis lines it up and whips it away with complete authority. It is going, going and travels all the way over deep mid-wicket. The lead goes up past 100 runs and the 100-run stand comes up as well. It has come at a brisk pace too. Both of them are putting their foot down.
Back of a length ball, angling in, Mendis defends it stoutly.
Spinning in nicely, defended solidly off the front foot.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads.
Fuller in length, played with soft hands towards mid on.
Stays back and tucks it to short leg.

Was there an edge? Seems like there wasn't. Tossed up delivery, takes off after pitching. Chandimal tries to ride the bounce and cut it away but gets beaten. Dowrich tries to take it with a hop but fails to do so. The Ultra Edge doesn't spot anything.
Chase spots Chandimal moving in his crease and bowls it around his pads. He tries to work it away but fails to do so and is hit on the pads.

Good fielding! Every run matters in a close contest. Shortish ball and room on offer, the batsman slaps it towards Roston Chase at backward point, who dives to his left and saves certain runs for his side.
Good length ball well outside off, punched off the back foot towards cover-point.
That one shoots off! Back of a length ball outside off, seams away with extra bounce. Mendis has a poke at it but is beaten all ends up.
Similar delivery, this time outside off. Kusal goes at it with hard hands but finds the man at covers.
FOUR! Nice positive stuff from Kusal Mendis! Fractionally overpitched around off, Mendis drives it crisply through wide mid on and finds the fence. He is looking really good.
In the channel outside off, Mendis lets it go.
No Ball! Lands it on a length well outside off, left alone. Roach has overstepped by a big margin.
Kemar Roach to bowl from the other end.
Gets behind and defends it nicely.
Two Byes! Floated one down the leg side. Keeper fails to collect it. Two runs taken.
Hangs back in his crease and blocks it out.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot.
Similar delivery around middle, defends it to the on side.
We are set to get underway. Kusal Mendis and Dinesh Chandimal to resume their innings. Roston Chase to bowl first up after Lunch.
Roston Chase starts with a loopy delivery around off, punched to the mid on region for a single.

Update 1240 Local - There was a brief passage of shower during the lunch break. However, the weather has brightened up and there is a bit of sunshine as well. Ian Bishop on air informs us that we will probably get underway in about 10 minutes. Be with us...
... Day 4, Session 2 ...

Amidst all this, Mendis has gone past a fifty. He has settled down and is getting good support from his skipper. The visitors lead by 89 and are placed nicely at the moment. The hosts need to find their mojo back to stay afloat. Join us shortly for the afternoon session.

However, the fortunes turned in the second half. The pair of Chandimal and Mendis took on Devendra Bishoo and scored some brisk runs. There was an instance when Mendis was caught off a no ball and there was a particular over from Shannon Gabriel which could still have a huge impact on this game. He got the better of the Sri Lankan skipper twice but once it was an illegal delivery and on another occasion the hosts didn't opt for the review. Such small events can make a lot of difference.

Session highlights - 31 overs, 102 runs, 3 wickets. It has been a really absorbing and eventful period of play. The first half belonged to the Windies hands down. Gabriel came out with aggressive intent and gave his side a couple of early breakthroughs to push the visitors on the back foot. He was well-supported by Roach who picked up a wicket as well.
Short of a length around off, Chandimal gets behind the line and defends it down the ground. THAT'S LUNCH ON DAY 4!

Chandimal is riding his luck and how! Another peach from Gabriel, pitching around off and straightening after pitching. Dinesh plays for the line but he is beaten all ends up. It was a whisker away from the edge and the off pole. So close and yet so far for Gabriel. Sri Lankan skipper survives, once again.
Outside off and left alone by the batsman.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Chandimal hops and keeps the incoming short delivery down. Four more balls to negotiate.
Back of a length around off, Chandimal blocks it from his crease.
Loopy around middle, defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Hangs back and blocks it to the bowler.
In the air... but no one there to pouch it. Mendis sweeps the flighted delivery towards fine leg. The fielder at square leg runs to his right and cuts it down to two.
Hangs back and dabs it to the left side of the fielder at short leg.
Comes in with the angle and blocked off the front foot for nothing.

6th Test fifty for Mendis! He has looked solid and finally converted it into something substantial. But it's still not over yet. Gets a flatter delivery around leg and he flicks it through backward square leg for a couple. This has been a crucial knock from him and he gets a pat on the back from his skipper.
Deep mid-wicket in place now.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.

AAH! Dicey from Mendis. He needs to be careful with these incoming deliveries. Gabriel has troubled the batsman throughout with such deliveries and he bowls another one. The ball lands around off and comes in with the angle. Mendis tries to flick it off his pads but gets it from the inside half of the bat. The ball rolls to the square leg region and one run is taken.
On a driveable length and asking to be hit. Mendis throws his bat at it, gets a thick outside edge and the ball goes between gully and point. Two more runs are added to the total.
Dishes this one fuller around off and the batsman punches it from the face of the bat. The ball goes past the umpire and two more runs are added to the total.
Similar delivery from Gabriel and blocked off the front foot by Mendis.
Back of a length around middle and leg, Chandimal tucks it to square leg. One run added to the total.
FOUR! Floater on middle, Mendis comes down the track and picks it up to hit it over the mid-wicket fielder. A boundary to end the over.
Driven through mid off by the batsman.
Flatter on leg, Chandimal works it to fine leg for a single.
Some extra bounce for Chase. Batsman comes forward to the flighted delivery but gets wrapped on his pads.
Loopy around middle, Mendis plays it to mid-wicket for nothing.
Again short and on to the stumps, Mendis tucks it to the leg side and takes a single. Mendis moves into the forties.
Another full ball and driven nicely to covers for nothing.
Full outside off and on a driveable length, Chandimal pushes it to covers with a straight bat.
Goes fuller and the ball jags back in. The batsman looks to cut but gets an under edge. No harm done.
Back of a length around middle and off. Blocked by Chandimal.
Bouncer! The batsman ducks in time to let that one go over him.
Yorker to start with. Chandimal manages to keep it out.
Hangs back and pushes it to the off side. One run results.
OOH! Extra bounce once again and jumps from the length area. Chandimal does well to keep it down to the off side.
He is guilty of bowling it short and Chandimal gets inside the line and nudges it fine. Two more runs are taken from the fine leg region.
Not the line he wants to work on. Another legsider and clipped to the leg side. One run added to the total.
Touch short around off, Chandimal goes back and cuts through point for another single.
Flatter down the leg side and swept to square leg for a single.
Roston Chase takes over from Devendra Bishoo.

Pitched up delivery, Chandimal goes at it with hard hands but mistimes it down the track. End of a very eventful over. Gabriel got Chandimal twice but once they didn't go for the review and on another occasion it was an illegal delivery.
Dinesh tries to flick that one but misses as the ball goes towards the keeper.
Fullish delivery, played with soft hands to mid off.

Caught off a no ball! Nothing is going right for the Windies. It was a terrific delivery but what a pity! Gabriel has overstepped. Great presence of mind from Mendis who suggested that the bowler has overstepped. Shortish delivery, takes off after pitching. Chandimal is caught in a tangle as he tries to fend it off but the ball hits the splice of his bat and lobs towards the gully region. Shai Hope takes it with ease and is all smiles. However, Mendis walks towards his skipper and stretches his right arm out. Umpire Ian Gould spots that and goes upstairs to check for the no ball. Well, Gabriel's front foot is way ahead of the popping crease when it lands. Chandimal gets a second life in a space of three deliveries. He will be thanking his stars.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.

So close but yet so far! Brilliant bowling from Gabriel. He goes a bit wider of the crease and angles in a full length ball on middle and leg. Chandimal attempts to drive it down the ground but seems to have got an inside edge onto his pads. The Windies appeal in unison but the umpire stays put. Holder doesn't go for the review. Oh no! The hosts have missed a trick. The Ultra Edge doesn't spot a nick. The Hawk Eye rolls in now and there are three reds. Perhaps, the sound of the bat hitting the pad confused the home side and hence, they didn't challenge the decision. Chandimal is a lucky man.
Slants this one down the leg side, Dinesh tries to help it away but misses.
Shannon Gabriel is back on. He was breathing fire in the morning and will be aiming to replicate that once again before Lunch.
Floated on middle and leg, Mendis sweeps it away towards deep backward square leg. A couple of runs are taken.
Shorter in length, cut away towards point.
Similar delivery, milked down to the same region for a run.
Tossed up ball, Kusal clears his front leg and knocks it down to long off for an easy run.
Drifting in on middle and leg, defended solidly off the front foot.

FOUR! The Sri Lankans are taking on the spinner! This is good aggressive batting. On a flatter trajectory around off, Mendis picks the length up in a jiffy and pulls it with aplomb over mid-wicket to find the fence.
Gets behind the back of a length delivery and keeps it out.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Flicks to square leg and changes strike.

Four Byes! Not good from the Windies skipper. Serves it on a fullish length on leg and it moves further away after pitching. Dowrich behind the stumps moves to his left but can't stop the ball. In the end, four more runs for the visitors.

FOUR! Mendis is relentless. He is looking to score and rightly so. Holder bangs it in and angles the ball into the batsman who swivels and pulls the ball to the left of the short mid-wicket fielder. The ball races away to the boundary and the 50-run stand is up between the two.

Back of a length into the body, Chandimal hops and flicks it to short mid-wicket for a run. The fielder is quick to reach the ball and throws it at the non-striker's end. No backing up behind the stumps means the ball goes away and a couple of extra runs are taken.
FOUR! BOOM! Out of nowhere, Mendis decides to take on the flighted ball. Gets hold of it and flat bats it over the mid-wicket region for a boundary. Sri Lanka getting a move on.

WOW! The bounce in the pitch is troubling the batsmen. Bishoo floats it around off and the ball grips, turns and takes off from there. Chandimal looks to cut it but it goes from the upper edge and over the slip fielder. Three runs are taken from the third man region.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

Loopy delivery around off, Chandimal comes down the track once again and looks to play it over the bowler's head. The ball grips and turns away from the face of the bat and flies over the fielder at mid off from the outside half of the bat. Two runs are taken.
Gives charge to the flighted delivery and defends it down the pitch. Some intent from Skip!
Touch short outside off and the batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches it to the off side.
Similar back of a length around off and confidently defended off the back foot to end the over.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Back of a length around off, Mendis gets behind the line and blocks it.
OOH! Another one takes off from length. Chandimal does well to guide it the vacant fine leg region. One run added to the total.
Back of a length around off, Chandimal stays in his crease and defends it nicely.
Wide! Bumper but it is too high! The batsman ducks in time to let that one go over him.

Close shave! Chandimal shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot to covers. The non-striker thinks there's a single and runs. But Chandimal loudly denies him and sends him back. A direct hit but the batsman makes it home.
Conventional leg break around off, the batsman hangs back and taps it to point.
Quicker around off, Mendis drives it to covers for nothing.
Driven through the covers by the batsman.
Now Mendis comes dancing down the pitch and creams the flighted delivery through covers for a brace.
The batsman charges down the track and plays it to mid off for another run.
Touch short around middle and leg, Chandimal tries to work it to the leg side but hits the fielder at short leg. One run is taken.
Pitched right up there again, played with soft hands to the off side.
In the channel outside off, left alone.
Fuller in length, eased off the front foot to covers.
Almost, almost! On a driveable length outside off, Chandimal falls for the bait. Goes for an ambitious drive but the ball just goes past the outside edge of his bat. Could have easily edged that one.
Hangs back to the similar length ball and keeps it out with a straight bat.
Length delivery on middle and leg, defended solidly off the back foot  beside the pitch on the leg side.
Change of ends for Holder.
FOUR! Well played! That was not easy to play. Loopy delivery in line of the stumps, Mendis skips down the track and whips it against the spin through mid-wicket. A boundary results.
Straighter one from Bishoo, Mendis clips it straight to the short leg fielder.
Flatter in trajectory, spinning away. Chandimal has ample time to work it towards mid-wicket for a run.
Fuller in length on off, kept out watchfully.
Shorter in length, Chandimal rocks back and cuts it straight to the cover fielder.
Tossed up around off, defended solidly off the front foot.
Time for spin. Devendra Bishoo to roll his arm over now.
Strays down the leg side and Chandimal flicks it off his hips and takes a single.
Short and outside off, the batsman keeps it down to the leg side for nothing.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Short of a length around off and blocked it off the back foot nicely.
Bouncer! The batsman ducks under it at the last moment.
The ball is down the leg side but the batsman still goes after it and misses.
A short ball around off and the batsman pushes it mid-wicket. End of another eventful over.
Hangs back and defends it from his crease.
Outswinger around off, Mendis plays it to mid off for nothing.
Back of a length outside off, the batsman blocks it.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.

No ball! Was there a nick? Oh man! Holder has his arms on his waist. He seems disappointed and why shouldn't he be. It was an edge but the no ball saved Mendis. Holder dishes it on a good length on middle and leg. The angle takes it further down the leg side and an edge is induced. Dowrich collects it safely. His body language indicates that he knows it and so does the batsman. The wicket-keeper appeals confidently but as soon as he does that, the umpire has his right arm outstretched. Well, the replays show that Holder has overstepped. He is gutted with himself. The Ultra Edge confirms there was a nick. Mendis survives!
In the air... but safe! Short and into the body, Chandimal swivels and goes for the pull. It goes off the top edge to fine leg but the fielder was a bit too square. No harm done in the end.

Time for Drinks. The hosts have been relentless. They have bowled with a lot of discipline and have hardly given anything away. Sri Lanka, on the other hand, haven't shown enough application, losing three wickets this morning. A lot lies on the current pair of Mendis and Chandimal. They need to bat as long as possible and keep the scoreboard ticking as well. While, the Windies will be aiming to keep chipping away the wickets.

Risky! It was asking to be hit and Chandimal didn't shy away either. Plays the cover drive uppishly and just wide of the diving fielder there. The ball stops inside the fence and two runs are taken. End of an eventful over.
On a length around middle and off, flicked to the leg side for nothing.
Jumps from the length once again and hits Mendis on his thigh pad. Out of nowhere, the ball is troubling the batsmen.
Defended off the back foot to covers.
Fullish ball, angling down. Mendis goes for the flick but is hit on the pads. An appeal follows but nothing from the umpire. That was probably going down leg.

OUCH! That must have hurt. Cummins bowls an effort ball, pitches it on a short of a length around off and the ball flies off the pitch into the grille of Mendis. The batsman takes evasive action, tries to bring his bat in line but it hits him on his gloves and lobs in the air. It hangs there for a while and goes towards Shai Hope at gully. He doesn't go for the catch as he felt it was too far away. Mendis survives a scare.
On the pads once again and pushed to the leg side for nothing.
Defended off the front foot by Chandimal by presenting the full face of the bat.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Four Byes! Oh dear me! Full and down the leg side. It seams further away from the batsman as well as the diving keeper who tries his best but fails to save the boundary.
Lands it outside off, stays touch low, the batsman defends it off the back foot.
Bouncer! The batsman does well to evade it.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Plants his foot down the pitch and pushes the full ball to wide mid off. The fielder cuts it out and keeps it down to one.
Touch short, into the body and flicks it away to square leg for a single.
Confident defense from the batsman off the similar looking delivery.
Similar length just outside off, the batsman blocks it off the front foot.
Back of a length around off and middle, Mendis gets behind and blocks it down the  track.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Nice channel from Holder, probing the batsman outside off who defends it off the front foot.
Gets into the body of the batsman who blocks it off nicely.
Copy paste stuff from the bowler and the batsman.
Back of a length outside off, Chandimal gets on his toes and punches it to mid off for nothing.
Starts with a wide one outside off, left alone by the batsman.
Jason Holder comes in for a bowl.
Similar looking delivery from the bowler and Mendis gets behind the line to block it.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
On a good length outside off, Chandimal taps it to the vacant cover region and calls for an easy single.
Too straight and down the leg. Dowrich takes a tumbling catch.
Beautiful looking punch off the back foot from Chandimal. It is short and outside off and punched through cover-point. The fielder chases it and saves a couple.
Waits for it and flicks the short ball to the leg side. One run added to the total.
Hangs back and pushes it off the back foot for nothing.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.

Roach drags his length back outside off and another punch from Mendis. He gets on top of the bounce and places it through cover-point. The ball is stopped inside the boundary and three more runs added to the total.

FOUR! WOW! Power punch from Mendis. Another full ball around middle and leg, the batsman presents the full face of the bat and gets it from the middle. The ball races away to the long on fence. It didn't look that good a shot but the timing was immaculate.
Touch fuller around middle and leg, the batsman gets it past the fielder at mid-wicket and takes a single.
Back of a length outside off, left alone by Chandimal.
Wide outside off stump, the batsman leaves it alone.
Around off, the batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends it down the pitch.
Similar delivery from Cummins and Mendis flicks it towards fine leg for nothing.
Too straight on the hips, the batsman flicks it to the vacant square leg region and changes strike.
Back of a length around off, Chandimal plays it from his crease to the off side.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Miguel Cummins is into the attack.
The ball is way outside the off stump, easy leave for the batsman.
Full around leg, Mendis tries to flick it but misses as the ball brushes his pads and goes to the keeper.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Back of a length into the body, Chandimal flicks to square leg and opens his account.

OUT! BANG! Another one bites the St Lucian dust. A nothing shot from Udawatte. He was looking good out in the middle but couldn't hang on. Not an ideal start for him in Test cricket. Another full ball from Roach on off stump, pushed in and straightening after pitching. The batsman play an uppish drive but the ball goes straight to Devendra Bishoo at mid off, who takes a jumping catch. Sri Lanka are in some trouble. Meanwhile, the skipper, Dinesh Chandimal walks out to bat.
Full around off, punched to the point region for nothing.
Too wide and another leave to end the over.
Full outside off, punched to the off side for nothing.
In the same channel outside off. He needs to come closer to the batsman to make full use of the new ball.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Too wide to entice the batsman. Perhaps a set up?? Let's see.
Wide outside off, left alone for the keeper.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full around middle, the batsman flicks it through the mid-wicket region and takes three. Sri Lanka are into the lead now.
On a good length just outside off and close to the bat but misses the outside edge of the blade. Tentative from Mendis.
Touch fuller outside off, Mendis gets it behind point from the outer half.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Back of a length on the hips, the batsman flicks it to mid-wicket and changes strike.
Kusal Mendis strides out to bat.

OUT! In that probing channel again and the result is the same. Gabriel has his man and Devon Smith who had dropped Chandimal in the first innings doesn't spill it this time and collects it cleanly to his left. Another delivery well outside off, on a driveable length and de Silva tries to push it through the line with minimal feet movement. The ball holds its line and an outside edge is induced. Smith at first slip pouches it safely. Sri Lanka lose their third wicket and trail by 3 runs. Great start to the day for the hosts.
Nice channel from Gabriel. Keeping it around off from back of a length and making the batsman have a feel for it.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Enticing full ball outside off, de Silva goes for it without any foot movement and drags it down the pitch for nothing.
Drags his length back, angles into his body and Mahela gets it to square leg from the inside half of the bat for a single.
Full and on middle, the batsman digs it out back to the bowler.
Short of a length around off, de Silva feels for it and gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Stays put in his crease and plays it to the off side.
Back of a length on middle and leg, Udawatte flicks to the leg side and changes strike. Trail is down to four now.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Roston Chase comes in at silly mid on.

High elbow and straight bat, nice and easy from de Silva. Gets a full ball outside off and punches it through covers. The fielder from covers cuts it inside the boundary with some handy footwork. In the end, three runs added to the total.
Full around off, Mahela pushes it off the front foot to vacant cover region and takes a single.
Wide outside off and takes off after landing. The keeper is unable to collect it cleanly but no harm done.
Copy past stuff from the bowler and the batsman.
On a good length around off, de Silva presents the full face of the bat.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
This one bounces nicely. Similar length into the batsman, he blocks it off the back foot.
OOH! It stayed a touch. Back of a length outside off, de Silva goes for the cut but the ball goes below the bat.
Goes full on middle and leg, Udawatte blocks it to the leg side for nothing.
Outside off, left alone.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
FOUR! Full, angling in and punched off the front foot down the pitch. The timing is good and the ball races to the long on fence for the first boundary of the day.
Full around off, pushed to the point fielder for nothing.
Starts from around the wicket and stays close to the off stump. Mahela blocks it from the crease to the off side.
Kemar Roach to bowl from the other end.
Gets behind the line and defends it off the back foot.
Outside off and left alone by the new batsman.
Dhananjaya de Silva comes out to bat.

OUT! Gabriel tastes first blood with just the fourth ball of the day. Lands it on a fuller length and brings it in with the angle. The ball skids after pitching and wraps him on his pads. Rajitha tries to get his bat down but he's late. The Windies go up in appeal and the umpire obliges after a bit of thinking. He bowled it at 145 kph, an effort ball from Gabriel and he has got the desired result.
Similar line and length, another leave from the nightwatchman.
Jags back in from back of a length, Rajitha keeps his bat down and moves away from the line.
Start with a gentle loosener outside off, left alone by Rajitha.
We are set to get underway. Mahela Udawatte and Kasun Rajitha to resume their innings. Shannon Gabriel to bowl first up this morning. Here we go...

PITCH REPORT - Jeff Dujon assessing the surface says that it has dried up and the cracks have opened up as well. Mentions that the good length area is posing problems for the batsmen and they have to be careful.

After a controversial third day, we are moving into the penultimate day with much abuzz. Sri Lanka will feel that they have an upper hand after their exploits yesterday, while Windies will be banking on their bowling to come good. The onus is on Kemar Roach and company to make use of the pitch which still has something in it and get through the defenses of the visiting batsmen. The match hangs in the balance for now, and the first session itself could decide the fate. Should be another exciting contest to watch. Stay tuned for live action.

Hello and welcome to the coverage of the fourth day of the second Test match between West Indies and Sri Lanka in St Lucia. To start the day, the news coming in from the centre is that Dinesh Chandimal has been charged for breaching 2.2.9 of the ICC code of conduct, which relates to tampering with the condition of the ball. The video from Day 2 shows Chandimal taking something out of his left pocket and putting it in his mouth. He immediately gets his finger to his mouth and uses it to shine the ball.
... Day 4, Session 1 ...

From the point of view of the hosts, half centuries from Devon Smith and Shane Dowrich allowed them to sneak past the away side's total. The pitch seems to have eased down a bit as well, making batting relatively easier. The first hour of Day 4 holds the key as to which side the game will tilt. Join us to catch all the action on Sunday. Till then, Ciao!

The umpires are having a discussion and the play has been called off for the day. It's STUMPS ON DAY 3! Kusal Perera and debutant Mahela Udawatte managed to get through the initial 30 minutes of play but the former lost his wicket just the way he did in the first innings. However, it's a passage of play which belonged to Sri Lanka, for the first time in this series. Their bowlers came out all guns blazing after the Tea break and took the winds out of the Windies lower order. Four out of the five bowlers chipped in with wickets and managed to keep the lead down to 47. They were quite disciplined throughout and didn't allow the home side to run away with the show.

Not Out! The hosts lose a review! A very good decision from Aleem Dar. Cummins bowls a good length ball around leg stump and tries to angle it across Udawatte. He hops in an attempt to block it but misses to get hit on the pads. A strong appeal follows but the umpire shakes his head. Holder after a conversation with his teammates decides to challenge the decision. Time for the replays. The Ultra Edge doesn't detect anything. The Hawk Eye rolls in. Well, the ball has pitched outside the leg stump and that puts the argument to bed.
The Windies review an LBW decision against Mahela Udawatte. Seems to be a close call but the height might just save him.

Just wide of the man at gully! Not a good shot to play at the fag end of the day. Fullish ball well outside off, Udawatte throws his bat at it and gets a thick outside edge. Hope at gully dives to his left but the ball goes past him in a flash. A couple of runs are taken.
The artificial lights have been switched on.
The batsman has played it towards mid-wicket.
Cummins delivers this on a length outside off, Mahela points his bat skywards to let it be.
Another bouncer which is comfortably evaded by Mahela with a duck.
Short ball on leg stump, Udawatte ducks under it.
After the blow near the knee, Kasun Rajitha is getting his leg checked by the physio. Meanwhile, Miguel Cummins comes into the attack.
Good length ball, nipping in sharply to go past Rajitha's pads to hit him on the thigh pads.
On a length outside off, left alone.
The nightwatchman, Kasun Rajitha walks out to bat. Still no signs of stumps, the play has probably been extended.

OUT! Got him, gone! Gabriel draws first blood. He wasn't looking that convincing with the ball but has produced a beauty to give his side the breakthrough. He steams in from around the wicket and hits the deck hard on middle. Perera plays for the initial angle but after pitching, the ball seams away late to catch him off guard. An outside edge is induced and Shane Dowrich behind the stumps gets low to his left to take a good catch. Perera's chancy innings has been cut short.
Gabriel has lost the plot once again. Slips this one down the leg side, Perera lets it go.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman.

Tight but safe eventually! Length ball, Perera places it towards mid off and calls his partner through. The fielder has a shy at the striker's end but misses. An overthrow results. Good game awareness from the Sri Lankans.
Well, we will get another over in.
FOUR! Crisp! Fuller length ball on off, Mahela Udawatte offers the full face of the bat and punches it through mid on to find the fence.
Pitched up this time, Udawatte puts his head down and defends it calmly down the pitch.
On a length around off, defended from within the crease.
Tight stump-to-stump line from the skipper. Mahela looks a bit nervy but manages to keep it out.
Full length ball attacking the stumps, the batsman plays it defensively beside the pitch on the leg side.
Holder comes around the wicket to change things up and lands the ball on a length outside off. Udawatte shuffles a touch and leaves it alone.
No ball! Slower ball outside off, doesn't bounce much as Mahela sees it through. Well, Holder has overstepped. Needs to be more disciplined.
Wide! Starts off with a shortish ball way outside off. Udawatte is not bothered to play at it.
This might well be the last over of the day. The skipper, Jason Holder brings himself on. Can he provide his side a breakthrough?
Tentative! In the channel of uncertainty, Perera tries to work it away but is hit on the thigh pad.
Back of a length ball, defended stoutly off the back foot.
A short leg in place now.
No ball! Bowls this one short down the leg side, Perera lets it go. Gabriel has overstepped as he was striving for extra pace. This is also Sri Lanka's highest opening partnership of this series.
FOUR! Streaky runs! Not that wide from Gabriel but it is too short. Perera rises on his toes and flashes at it only to top edge it over the slip cordon. A boundary results.
Makes good use of the crease does Gabriel. He goes wide and angles in a short of a length ball. Perera is cramped for room as he tries to manufacture a glide through point but is beaten for pace.
Short of a length ball in line of the stumps, tucked with a closed bat face towards wide mid on. A single taken.
Beaten! One of the few deliveries he has got up there after a sequece of short ones. Udawatte comes forward tentatively and pushes at it tamely only to get foxed.
Hangs back to the length ball and answers it with a straight bat.
Bowls this one in the tight off stump channel. Perera chances his arms and tries to hit it down the ground but mistimes it over the bowler. A couple of runs is the result.
Roach bowls this one closer to the stumps. The batsman with a still head defends it with authority.
Short of a length outside off, Kusal Perera shuffles a touch and taps it towards cover-point.
This one is wide outside off and this time Perera restricts himself as he lets it go.

This is the fag end of the day but Perera is still taking some risks. Don't think this is the right approach. Fractionally overpitched outside off, Kusal tries to whack it over covers but gets beaten.
A play and a miss! Back of a length and width on offer. Udawatte tries to slash it over point but only connects with thin air.
Shortish delivery aimed at the body. Kusal pulls it through square leg to rotate strike.
Makes use of the depth of the crease and turns this one towards mid-wicket for a single.
Gabriel is struggling with his rhythm. Angles the shortish delivery down the leg side as Udawatte points his bat skywards to let it be.
Back of a length delivery in that probing off stump corridor. Mahela shuffles a touch and defends it with a straight bat.
On a good length around off, Perera punches it towards point where Chase dives full strectch to his left to make a good stop. A tight single taken.
Lets one through to the keeper.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
OOH! What a comeback from Roach! Brings it closer to the batsman and makes him go for the delivery. On a full length outside off and Mahela goes for the cover drive but misses.
Similar line and length and batsman ignores it once again.
Too wide and another leave from Mahela.
Full ball outside off and left alone by the batsman.
Similar delivery around the hips, helped away to fine leg for a single.
Gabriel once again loses his radar and slips this one down the leg side.
The batsman works it down the leg side.
Shortish delivery, angling down leg. Mahela tries to glance it but misses.
Udawatte avoids a pair and gets his first runs in Test cricket! A sigh of relief for him. Fullish ball outside off, stroked nicely through wide mid off for a brace.
Short of a length ball outside off, played with an angled bat to point.
Shannon Gabriel to share the new ball from the other end.
FOUR! Hammered! Perera is going with the flow. Back of a length ball outside off, doesn't bounce much. Perera flat-bats it through mid off for a rocketing boundary. 10 from the first over.

That was so close! Perera has come out with an aggressive mindset but that can well backfire. Fullish length ball just outside off, Perera attempts a heave across the line but misses. The ball misses the off stump by a whisker.
Short of a length outside off, punched nicely through covers for a couple.

FOUR! Brilliant shot to get underway! That will give him a lot of confidence. Full length ball on middle and off, Perera lines it up and whips it over square leg for a boundary. The bottom hand came into play there.
Well bowled! Lands it on a similar length and gets the ball to skid after pitching. Kusal tries to work it away but is hit on the thigh pad.
Kemar Roach runs in from around the wicket and bowls it in the avenue of apprehension. Perera shuffles a touch and blocks it right under his eyes.
